results.rationale: No supporting or refuting evidence is attached to this hypothesis, so there is nothing in the evidence record that contradicts the stated actor, place, mechanism, or interval. An empty evidence set is not itself a contradiction, so the hypothesis stands unrejected by default. (Note, model-prior: gamma-ray-ionization is an unusual mechanism to pair with a Taurid-swarm actor, which is conventionally linked to airburst/impact mechanisms rather than radiative ones, but this is plausibility commentary only, not an evidence-based contradiction.)
No supporting or refuting evidence is listed for this placement, so no concrete contradiction exists in the record regarding actor, object, place, mechanism, or interval.
No evidence is attached. The stated interval [-11000,-10001] is broad and consistent with the Younger Dryas boundary timing (~-10950) used elsewhere in this evidence set, so nothing contradicts it.

The evidence listed under 'Refuting evidence' (Boslough 2012, Daulton 2010, Haile 2009, Holliday 2014, Paquay 2009, Surovell 2009) all describe independent replication failures, absence of geochemical/physical signatures, and gradual rather than catastrophic extinction — these findings actually corroborate rather than contradict this hypothesis's own claim that the cosmic-impact explanation for megafaunal extinction is 'refuted' via independent-replication-failure. No item in the evidence contradicts the actor, place, mechanism, or interval as stated.

The refuting evidence (Paquay 2009) reports no chondritic iridium enrichment at Younger Dryas boundary sediments across multiple sites, which supports rather than contradicts this hypothesis's claim that the iridium-anomaly attribution to cosmic-impact is refuted. The evidence text does not specify a location that excludes North America, nor does it state an explicit date range that is incompatible with the hypothesis's stated interval [-13000,-12001], so no concrete contradiction is established by the evidence itself. (Model-prior note: other hypotheses in this set place the Younger Dryas boundary near -10950, which sits outside this hypothesis's stated interval — a possible chronological inconsistency worth flagging for review, but not a contradiction stated within this hypothesis's own attached evidence.)

The supporting evidence (Brakenridge 2011) describes ice-core beryllium-10 and nitrate spikes near the Pleistocene-Holocene transition proposed as consistent with supernova-driven ionizing radiation, matching the actor, mechanism, 'inconclusive' status, and interval. The evidence frames this as an alternative trigger for the 'terminal Rancholabrean extinction pulse' rather than explicitly for 'younger-dryas-onset-cooling,' which is a minor object-framing mismatch, but this is not a concrete contradiction of place, time bin, or actor attestation as required for rejection.

The refuting evidence (van Hoesel 2014) concerns the Usselo horizon in the Netherlands (i.e., within Europe), finding the nanodiamond-bearing layer postdates the Allerod-Younger Dryas transition rather than coinciding with it — this supports rather than contradicts the hypothesis's own 'refuted' status for a synchronous impact-ejecta nanodiamond signal. Place (Europe) and mechanism (impact-ejecta-fallout) are consistent with the cited site and claim; no contradiction is present.

No supporting or refuting evidence is attached to this hypothesis, so nothing in the record contradicts the meltwater-pulse actor, megafaunal-extinction object, Greenland ice-sheet placement, dating-uncertainty mechanism, or the broad interval given.
